title: A simple model of AI-aided economic growth - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Tyler Cowen proposes replacing the Solow model with a two-factor model of Intelligence (formal smarts, now massively boosted by AI) and Polanyi knowledge (tacit, local, inarticulable know-how where humans specialize), which are mostly complements with limited substitutability. The core prediction is that the AI shock to Intelligence raises marginal returns, employment and real wages in the Polanyi sector slowly but persistently, while transitional unemployment hits the Intelligence sector once Centaur models fade — and it implies that commandeering the Intelligence sector yields far less societal power than it appears.

insights.claim: The Solow model fails for major AI-driven changes; a better framework treats output as produced by two factors, Intelligence (chess, proving theorems, evals) and Polanyi knowledge (knowledge of time and place, inarticulable knowledge, custom and habit), which are mostly complements rather than substitutes.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A reusable macro frame for pricing AI's growth impact — bottlenecks sit in tacit-knowledge sectors, not in compute or model quality.
insights.quote: Intelligence and Polanyi knowledge are not quite Leontief complements, but they are mostly complements.
insights.locator: The Solow model has its uses

insights.claim: AIs cannot yet be brought into an office and made to figure out how that office works in the human rather than purely mechanistic sense, so Polanyi knowledge production remains human-specialized even though AI can aid it.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Explains why enterprise AI deployment lags model capability — the integration bottleneck is organizational, which slows realized productivity gains and the revenue ramp for AI vendors.
insights.quote: there is no way you can “bring an AI into your office and have it figure out how that office works.”

insights.claim: Substitutability between the two factors is limited and can be negative in effect: a dose of AI-drenched technocratic knowledge does not solve office norms problems and sometimes makes them worse by further empowering rent-seekers.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Flags a real downside channel where AI adoption degrades rather than improves organizational output — a source of disappointing enterprise ROI.
insights.quote: Sometimes it even can make those problems worse, by empowering rent-seekers further.

insights.claim: The core prediction of the model is that the huge positive shock to US Intelligence raises marginal returns, employment and real wages in the Polanyi knowledge sector, because its inputs are now relatively scarce compared with the enlarged quantity of Intelligence.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Long tacit-knowledge-intensive labor and services; the wage upside accrues to roles that require local, relational and contextual know-how rather than formal reasoning.
insights.quote: The core prediction is that this increases marginal returns, employment, and real wages in the Polanyi knowledge sector.

insights.claim: There will be transitional unemployment in the Intelligence sector once Centaur (human-plus-AI) models fade, though so far Centaur models are holding — mathematicians did the prompting for the new math work — with the chess trajectory as the template for eventual fade.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Watch the persistence of human-in-the-loop arrangements as the leading indicator for white-collar displacement timing.
insights.quote: There will also be some transitional unemployment in the Intelligence sector, at least once Centaur models fade.
insights.locator: There will also be some transitional unemployment

insights.claim: The Polanyi sector cannot be boosted quickly or with direct and simple efficacy because it is messy by nature, so wage and employment gains there arrive slowly but keep coming for a long period as further AI advances land and prior advances get absorbed.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Implies a long, drawn-out productivity diffusion rather than a step change — argues against near-term explosive-growth trades and for duration in AI-adjacent services.
insights.quote: It is messy by its nature, to cite a term from Luis Garicano.
insights.locator: Note that the Polanyi sector cannot be boosted

themes.theme: Power concentration and the growth path

insights.claim: If someone or something could commandeer the Intelligence sector, their power over society would be much more limited than it first appears, because the necessary Polanyi complements are lacking and the world does not change much at first.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Undercuts both AI-takeover tail scenarios and the winner-take-all case for whoever controls frontier models — control of intelligence is not control of output.
insights.quote: if someone or something could “commandeer” the Intelligence sector, their power over society would be much more limited than it might appear at first
insights.locator: In this model, if someone or something

insights.claim: The model is claimed to already match the data: shocking AI and tech advances alongside a job market that is doing fine, markets not pricing high risk, and economic growth that is robust rather than exploding but likely to rise in the future.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Supports a base case of gradually rising growth with contained risk premia, rather than either an AI bust or an imminent growth explosion.
insights.quote: we have shocking AI and tech advances, the job market is doing fine, markets do not see high risk, and economic growth is robust, not exploding, but likely will rise in the future
insights.locator: This very simple model so far is matching up

insights.claim: The Solow model usually works because it is rare for the Intelligence sector to swing upward so rapidly, keeping cross-sector ratios and complementarities roughly constant in the short run — a condition explicitly said not to hold in 2026 or in the next years.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Standard growth-accounting forecasts are mis-specified for this regime; expect consensus models to miss on both the composition and timing of AI-era growth.
insights.locator: The Solow model usually does fine
